newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls for education effort for capital.
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls for education effort for capital.

text.p: President Clinton Friday visited an inner city Washington elementary school, where he read "The Tortoise and the Hare" to class of first graders and called for better education in the capital city.

"Good morning President Clinton and Mrs. Clinton," said the 19-member class of 6- and 7-year-olds as the president and first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton entered the classroom at Garrison Elementary School.

Clinton was pushing a programme to recruit university students to act as individual reading tutors for children. Seven universities in Washington have pledged to join the effort and 42 tutors were already active at Garrison.
Clinton wants every American child to be able to read independently by the age of 8 but four out of 10 currently fall short of the required standard.
The children sang Clinton a song, "I believe I can fly, I believe I can touch the sky. If I can read I can fly."

Then the president and first lady read the fable of how the slow and steady tortoise won the race against the speedy hare and explained that they should stick to their studies even if they were hard and progress was slow.
"Have you got a nice house?" one of the children asked Mrs. Clinton. "Yes we do. Have any of you ever visited the White House? That's where we live," she replied.

Later in a speech to Washington civic leaders who gathered in the school, Clinton repeated his commitment to try to lift standards in Washington, where the education system, as well as the city finances, were in crisis.

"This endeavour will require us to be more like the tortoise than the hare. We will have to move slowly but deliberately and we will not be able to sit down and rest," Clinton said. "But if we do that, like the tortoise we will win the race."
Clinton has sent Congress a proposal to ease the financial plight of Washington but it has received a chilly reception from some in the Republican majority.
Criticised for ignoring the city during his first term, Clinton has been more vocal in recent weeks about the need to revitalise Washington.
"I pledge to you today that we, my personal family and my official family, will be with you as you make these efforts every step of the way," Clinton said.

He said the two top priorities for Washington were making the schools work and the streets safe. "This is not going to be done overnight. Children are not built in a day. But it is a very important start," Clinton said.
